entry.title: IceCube Nobel Prize
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Royal Swedish Academy of Science announced the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for Francis Halzen, principal investigator of IceCube, for decisive contributions to the observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. Wisconsin Public Radio interviewed Halzen about the prize and the importance of neutrino research. KM3NeT sent congratulations, and the South Pole station gathered at the IceCube Lab for a celebratory photo.

entry.title: KM3NeT construction
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. KM3NeT was recognised as a Landmark in the ESFRI Roadmap 2026, the European strategy forum's list of major research infrastructures. In marine operations reported on 9 October, Cable Termination Frame 3 was installed at the ARCA deep-sea site. The same report describes a further step for ORCA, but the record excerpt does not give its details.

entry.title: JUNO-TAO
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Taishan Antineutrino Observatory is a satellite of JUNO. It measures the reactor antineutrino spectrum at a baseline of 43.2 m with a 2.8-ton liquid-scintillator detector read out by 4,024 silicon photomultiplier tiles. Installation was completed in 2025 and physics data taking began on 10 February 2026. The JUNO Collaboration reports stable cryogenic operation, with about 90% of the readout channels retained.

entry.title: P-ONE photomultipliers
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. P-ONE is a planned cubic-kilometre-scale neutrino telescope for the Pacific Ocean, using Ocean Networks Canada infrastructure. Its first detector line will carry 320 three-inch Hamamatsu R14374-10 photomultiplier tubes. A new article characterises all the tubes to be integrated into that line before deployment, to check compliance with the detector acceptance criteria.

entry.title: Baikal-GVD sources
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Baikal-GVD, a cubic-kilometre-scale detector under construction in Lake Baikal, is now 70% complete. A search for point-like astrophysical neutrino sources used a five-year track-like dataset from 2019-2024. No significant source was found, so upper limits were computed for selected candidate objects and compared with IceCube, ANTARES and KM3NeT results.

entry.title: T2K near detector
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The upgraded ND280 includes SuperFGD, a segmented scintillator detector of about 2 million optically isolated 1 cm³ cubes. Its performance in the T2K beam is described in one paper. A second paper presents an event selection for muon-neutrino charged-current interactions with single positively charged pion production in the new modules, noting that the upgrade was completed in 2024. The selection targets the interaction-modelling uncertainties that limit T2K's oscillation analysis.

entry.title: IceCube infrared flares
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. An IceCube search for high-energy neutrinos from infrared flares is motivated by the neutrino emission seen from TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 and by external candidate associations such as AT2019dsg and AT2019fdr. The record excerpt does not state the outcome of the search.

entry.title: NνDEx simulation
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. NνDEx is planned for the China Jinping Underground Laboratory. It will search for neutrinoless double beta decay of 82Se using a high-pressure gas time projection chamber filled with 82SeF6 and read out by a Topmetal pixel system. A new paper presents a full simulation and reconstruction framework for it, built on the REST software toolkit.

entry.title: The paper examines the contribution of Δ-isobar direct-Urca processes to neutrino emissivity in neutron stars
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper examines the contribution of Δ-isobar direct-Urca processes to neutrino emissivity in neutron stars. The record states that this contribution had not been explicitly determined, although nucleonic and hyperonic Urca processes are known to be dominant cooling mechanisms. It matters for the thermal evolution of massive neutron stars if they contain Δ isobars.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors compute two-neutrino double beta decay rates with the full interdependence of nuclear structure and lepton kinematics, rather than decoupling them. They show deviations from closure, non-closure and Taylor-expansion treatments for 82Se and 136Xe. This is relevant to the modelling of rates and electron spectra for these isotopes.

entry.title: The paper uses a gauged Lμ-Lτ model with an ultralight vector boson that mixes kinetically with the photon
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper uses a gauged Lμ-Lτ model with an ultralight vector boson that mixes kinetically with the photon. This produces an extra matter potential in the Sun and so modifies MSW flavour conversion. It uses Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande solar measurements and discusses prospects for JUNO and XLZD.

entry.title: The authors study thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, where neutrino masses arise from
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors study thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, where neutrino masses arise from a dimension-7 operator at tree level and a dimension-5 operator at one loop. The model gives sub-eV neutrino masses with new physics near the TeV scale. The paper asks whether leptogenesis works in this setting, which differs from canonical seesaw leptogenesis.

entry.title: The paper asks whether neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae could be detected through nuclear
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper asks whether neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae could be detected through nuclear recoil tracks in ancient minerals (paleodetectors). It varies neutron-star masses, includes failed supernovae that form black holes, and considers the nuclear equation of state. Sensitivity is larger for models with larger neutrino emission.

entry.title: The paper considers magnetic and oscillation effects on neutrinos emitted from a protoneutron star in a supern
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper considers magnetic and oscillation effects on neutrinos emitted from a protoneutron star in a supernova. It reports that oscillations in the outer stellar layers harden the electron antineutrino spectrum, most strongly for the inverted mass ordering. That ordering dependence would favour ground-based detection of supernova neutrinos.
